state: Notes from the office move planning meeting.
Attendees were Priya, Tom, Lena and Marcus.
The new office is on the fourth floor of the Harbor building.
It has room for sixty desks and three meeting rooms.
Priya asked everyone to pack their desks by Friday 14 March.
Tom will arrange parking permits for the new site.
The old lease is with a company called Brandt Property.
Lena reminded the team that the kitchen is shared.
Coffee machines will move with the facilities crew.
Movers arrive at 8 a.m. on Saturday 15 March, so keys must be handed in by then.
Marcus asked about the cost of new chairs.
Chairs are budgeted at roughly two hundred each.
The meeting rooms will be named after local rivers.
Nobody has chosen a name for the largest room yet.
IT needs the list of monitors to be moved by Wednesday 12 March.
Cables will be labelled with colored tape.
Lena suggested a farewell lunch at the old office.
The lunch budget is small but enough for pizza.
Tom noted the lift at the new building is slow.
Stairs are fine for anyone going up one floor.
The old office must be fully empty and cleaned before 31 March, when the lease ends.
Priya will walk through the building with the landlord.
A cleaning company has already been booked.
Marcus will update the address on the website.
Business cards will be reprinted later in the spring.
The plants will move in Priya's car.
Everyone liked the view of the harbor from the new space.
The next meeting is not yet scheduled.
Tom closed the meeting with thanks to the team.
Notes written by Lena.
Greenfield Community Garden newsletter.
Welcome to a new season of growing.
This year we have forty-two plots, up from thirty-six.
The new plots are along the eastern fence.
Our compost bins are open to every member.
Plot fees of 25 dollars are due by 1 April to keep your spot.
Fees pay for water, seeds and tool repairs.
Please bring your own gloves to work days.
Sam found three kinds of beetles in the herb bed.
Most of them are harmless.
The tool shed has a new lock.
Collect your new key from the committee before 20 April or the lock cannot be opened.
Members who cannot garden this year should tell us.
Their plots may be offered to the waiting list.
The waiting list has eleven names.
Our annual seed swap was a great success.
We swapped over two hundred packets.
Tomatoes and beans were the most popular.
Sign up for a spring work day by 5 April, so we can plan the tasks.
Work days run on Saturday mornings.
Children are welcome with an adult.
The pond needs a new liner.
Volunteers have offered to help with that.
Thanks to everyone who donated wood chips.
The summer barbecue invitations go out on 1 June, and replies are needed by 15 June.
Last year's barbecue had grilled corn and peaches.
Vegetarian options are always included.
Do not forget to water on hot days.
The hose reel is next to the shed.
Happy growing from the committee!
